text:
ashley: heads-up: hosted API p99 spiked to ~1.8s for ~18min starting 02:28 UTC, baseline ~400ms. dashboards show queue depth climb on frontends and some long-lived priming requests. :rotating_light:
samir: looking now — traces show a burst of concurrent priming/backfill from tenant noisy-42 at 02:27. lots of small requests (1-3 tokens) interleaved with long-context priming -> batch fragmentation.
mike: can you paste the profiler snapshot? wondering if kernel selector flipped to aux frequently.
samir: grabbing profiling dump from runtime node a12: 
```
kernel_switch_count: 940
avg_batch_size: 2.2
kv_cache_evictions: 412
prefetch_requests/sec: 210
avg_latency_ms: 1820 (p99)
```
ashley: that kv_cache_evictions number stands out. could be thrash from backfill flood bumping prefetched prefixes out.
infra-bot: deployment "kselector-tuning" rolled out to cluster-3 at 01:50 UTC (successful).
nora: that rollout changed kernel weight heuristics to prefer fast-path primarily for <64 token flows. might be causing misselection for mixed-length workloads.
mike: hypothesis: rollout increased fast-path affinity, but long priming requests cause cache churn and small requests get degraded because kernel selection toggles and batches are tiny. leads to queue buildup and p99 spike.
oncall-ryan: traffic shaping shows ratecap didn't trip, but queue depth at frontend increased from 6->24 during spike window. rate limiter allowed backlog to form.
samir: checking tenant fingerprinting — noisy-42 had a scheduled backfill job at 02:20 (should have been off-peak). logs: "start backfill job: prefix-seed=0x7f, concurrency=40".
ashley: that explains bad mix. what's quick mitigation? pin kernel selector or bump batching window?
mike: immediate mitigation options: 1) revert kselector rollout (cluster-3) 2) increase batching coalesce window to 12ms 3) throttle noisy-42 at edge. best is edge throttle + batching bump.
samir: I can push a per-tenant ratecap for noisy-42 (limit concurrency to 6) and bump coalesce window on hosted runtime to 12ms. rolling now to canary subset.
infra-bot: config change: hosted-runtime.coalesce_ms=12 applied to canary nodes (a12,a13) at 02:46 UTC.
samir: applied tenant throttle for noisy-42 (concurrency=6) at 02:47.
nora: also pinning kselector to conservative mode on canary so kernel switching is reduced.
oncall-ryan: metrics: within 90s p95/p99 trending back down. queue depth on frontend dropped from 24->8.
nashley: nice work. let's keep monitoring and follow up with postmortem. immediate action: keep tenant throttle for 6h, revert rollout and schedule a controlled experiment for kselector with mixed-length workloads.
mike: logging action items: 
- revert kselector rollout in cluster-3 (owner: nora)
- run synthetic mixed-length load test with backfill pattern (owner: samir)
- add alert for kv_cache_evictions spikes tied to coalesce window changes (owner: mike)
- update runbook to include tenant backfill detection (owner: ashley)

ashley: tagging oncall-ryan for follow-up on SLA window. :thumbsup:
oncall-ryan: I'll keep 1h guard and start the runbook doc.
samir: leaving tracer snippets and flame baseline in the incident channel. small note: profiler showed a ~3x increase in kernel_switches during spike vs baseline (fast<->aux thrash). will add numbers to postmortem.
nora: good catch on rollout timing. scheduling a rollback of the kselector change and a phased re-eval with synthetic backfill next week.
ashley: closing the thread for triage; reopening if regressions. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
